League Division 2 season''' was the 39th season of the second-tier club football in Japan and the 12th season since the establishment of [[J2 League]]. The season began on March 6 and ended on December 4.{{cite web|url=http://japantoday.com/category/sports/view/j-league-to-kick-off-season-march-6|title=J-League to kick off season March 6}}{{Dead link|date=April 2019 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }} In this season, the number of participating clubs was increased by one, making the total number, nineteen. As opposed to the last two seasons, clubs will play double-round robin, instead of triple-round robin. At the end of the season, the top three clubs were promoted to [[J. League Division 1]] for the [[2011 J. League Division 1|2011 season]]. League Division 1|2009]] |- |[[Roasso Kumamoto]] |[[Kumamoto, Kumamoto|Kumamoto]], [[Kumamoto Prefecture|Kumamoto]] | |- |[[Sagan Tosu]] |[[Tosu, Saga|Tosu]], [[Saga Prefecture|Saga]] | |- |[[Thespakusatsu Gunma|Thespa Kusatsu]] |All cities/towns in [[Gunma]] | |- |[[Tochigi SC]] |[[Utsunomiya]], [[Tochigi Prefecture|Tochigi]] | |- |[[Tokushima Vortis]] |All cities/towns in [[Tokushima Prefecture|Tokushima]] | |- |[[Tokyo Verdy]] |All cities/towns in [[Tokyo]] | |- |[[Ventforet Kofu]] |All cities/towns in [[Yamanashi Prefecture|Yamanashi]] | |- |[[Yokohama FC]] |[[Yokohama]], [[Kanagawa Prefecture|Kanagawa]] | |} ==League format== Nineteen clubs will play in double round-robin (home and away) format, a total of 36 games each. A club receives 3 points for a win, 1 point for a tie, and 0 points for a loss. The clubs are ranked by points, and tie breakers are, in the following order: * Goal differential * Goals scored * Head-to-head results * Disciplinary points A draw would be conducted, if necessary. However, if two clubs are tied at the first place, both clubs will be declared as the champions. Three top clubs will be promoted to J1 (see below). ;Changes from Previous Year * Nineteen participating clubs, increased by one, [[Giravanz Kitakyushu]], from last year * Due to abolishment of triple round-robin format, which has been applied for the past two seasons, and installation of double round-robin, the number of games per club decreased to 36, down from 51, the fewest games played in J2, as same as [[1999 J. League Division 2|1999 J2 season]]. Therefore, regular season schedule had a month break after June 13 games during 2010 FIFA World Cup, first World Cup break as J2 since the [[2002 FIFA World Cup|2002 events held in Japan]], then the
